title: Removing Set Items
learningObjectives: Explain removing set items and when it is useful.
Use the relevant Python operations with correct syntax.
Predict the result of common operations and edge cases.
Distinguish mutation, return values and error behavior.
Apply the concept to a small data-processing task.

understand.concept: remove raises KeyError when the member is absent; discard does nothing in that case. pop removes and returns an arbitrary member, and clear empties the set. Do not rely on pop returning a particular element.
understand.whyItMatters: Removing Set Items is useful when a program needs to organize, inspect or transform related data reliably.
understand.analogy: A set is like a collection of unique membership cards: each item is present once, with no positional promise.
understand.analogyLimit: A set does not preserve a meaningful position for each member, and elements must be hashable.

explain.narrative:
## Removing Set Items

remove raises KeyError when the member is absent; discard does nothing in that case. pop removes and returns an arbitrary member, and clear empties the set. Do not rely on pop returning a particular element.

## Choosing an operation

Read the example code and check whether the operation mutates the object, returns a new value, or may raise an exception. Use membership tests and defaults where input may be missing.

## Practical reasoning

The five examples progress from basic use to a small real-world pattern. Compare each expected output with the code before changing it.

examples.title: Example 1: Removing Set Items
examples.explanation: remove deletes the specified existing member.

examples.title: Discard a missing member
examples.explanation: discard is safe when the member may be absent.

examples.title: Use pop without assuming order
examples.code:
values = {10}
removed = values.pop()
print(removed in {10})
print(len(values))
examples.explanation: pop returns and removes an arbitrary member; this singleton has only one choice.

examples.title: Clear a set
examples.explanation: clear removes all members from the existing set.

examples.title: Check before remove
examples.explanation: Membership testing prevents remove from raising KeyError.
